His father died when he was three. At 23 he left home to become a monk of the Lebanese Maronite Order and took the name Charbel. He was ordained a priest on July 23, 1859. For many years he lived in the community at the Monastery of Saint Maron at Annaya. From 1875 he lived as a hermit nearby, in prayer, fasting and manual work. He died on December 24, 1898, eight days after he was taken ill while celebrating Mass. Crowds came to his tomb afterward, Christians and Muslims alike. He studied Arabic, French and Syriac at the College de la Sagesse in Beirut, then went to Alexandria in 1892 to teach Arabic - and there, far from home, heard the call to the priesthood. The next year he entered the Capuchin convent of Khashbau, back in his own hills, and on November 1, 1901, he was ordained a priest in Beirut. Lebanon knew him simply as Abouna Yaacoub - Father Jacob. From 1903 to 1914 he walked Lebanon on foot with a knapsack on his shoulder, preaching in village after village - and became known as the Apostle of Lebanon . Bekaa Kafra sits at about 1,800 meters above sea level in the Bsharri district of North Lebanon - widely known as the highest village in the country. Its name is Syriac: bekaa , ground, and kafra , rich - "rich soil." It overlooks the holy valley of Qannoubine, which sheltered twenty-four Maronite patriarchs between 1440 and 1823 along with generations of hermits and monks, and it neighbors the Cedars of God. The village's own history reaches back at least to the tenth century by the historian Fouad Boustany Ephram's account, and its houses still keep their modest old architecture. Youssef Antoun Makhlouf was born here, traditionally on May 8, 1828, the youngest of five children of Antoun Zaarour Makhlouf and Brigitta Chidiac. Full Rosary Start The Rosary opens with the Apostles' Creed, one Our Father, three Hail Marys for faith, hope, and charity, and the Glory Be. You mark yourself with the Sign of the Cross, then say the Apostles' Creed - the short statement of what Christians believe. One Our Father follows, then three Hail Marys offered for faith, hope, and charity, and the Glory Be. Only then does the first decade begin. Each decade keeps the same shape: the mystery is announced, one Our Father, ten Hail Marys prayed slowly with the mystery in mind, and the Glory Be. The Fatima prayer closes each decade. When the fifth decade ends, the Rosary closes with the Hail Holy Queen and the concluding Rosary prayer. Opening: Sign of the Cross, Apostles' Creed, Our Father, three Hail Marys, Glory Be.
